//: The NODE side: server/, shared/, tests/, scripts/. The browser side has its own
project at web/tsconfig.json (Next owns that one, and it must NOT carry
exactOptionalPropertyTypes — it fights React prop spreading and Next's generated types).
The split is forced, not stylistic: shared/ is compiled by BOTH projects, so it can
contain no Node global and no DOM global. That is a structural guarantee that shared/
`erasableSyntaxOnly` is load-bearing. The server has NO build step — `node server/index.ts`
runs TypeScript via Node 24's native type stripping, which cannot execute enums,
namespaces, decorators, or constructor parameter properties. This flag turns each of
those into a compile error instead of a runtime crash at boot.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` follows from the same fact: every server-side relative
import ends in `.ts` because Node resolves the real file, not a compiled one.
